clue.text: All too human story in which evil makes a comeback

indicators.note: the story is said to hold the other piece inside it

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: coming back here means the word for evil is read from right to left

parts.note: ill can mean evil or harm, as in 'speak ill of'

explanation.surface: A tale about human weakness in which wickedness returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a comeback' turns ILL into LLI, and 'in which' puts that inside FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is human, so someone all too human is prone to mistakes.

clue.text: A word of twenty-six letters

parts.note: not a very long word but a single word naming the full set of twenty-six characters used in English writing

explanation.definitionFit: The English letter set has twenty-six members, and its name is one word.

clue.text: Have a great time-never mind the tears!

definitions.text: Have a great time-never mind the tears!

parts.words: Have a great time-never mind the tears!
parts.note: the idiom for acting without restraint, read literally as allowing things to tear, with 'tears' as rips rather than weeping

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for behaving with abandon, enjoying oneself without holding back.

clue.text: A well-filled vessel

parts.note: read as a container filled at a well, a pail lowered on a rope, rather than one that is generously full

explanation.definitionFit: A pail is the vessel lowered into a well to draw up water.

clue.text: Sheep to handle, we hear

indicators.note: the word for handle is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to use something is to handle or operate it

explanation.surface: Advice that sheep are to be handled, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: USE, from 'to handle', said aloud gives the plural of female sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are called by this word; a plural noun for the animals.

clue.text: Works of art produced from scratch

definitions.text: Works of art produced from scratch

parts.words: Works of art produced from scratch
parts.note: 'from scratch' usually means starting afresh, but here these prints are made by scratching lines into a metal plate

explanation.definitionFit: Prints made by incising a design into a plate with acid or a needle.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland

parts.note: looks like the name of the financial institution, but means a hillside or slope in Scots dialect

explanation.definitionFit: Scots word for a steep slope or hillside by a river.

clue.text: Apprentices the boss sent sprawling

parts.note: a boss is a knob or stud, as on a shield

indicators.note: the word sent is spread out untidily, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss scattering trainees about the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' turns SENT into ENTS, placed after STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners of any kind, people being taught a trade or subject.

clue.text: Treat raw spillage seen in the river

indicators.note: spilled things are scattered, so the letters of treat raw are reordered

explanation.surface: Untreated water has spilled and been spotted in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spillage' signals the anagram of TREAT RAW; the definition is a loose description of a riverbank creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole is a riverside rodent commonly spotted in British streams.

clue.text: Slight quarrel with father in the street

indicators.note: the father is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A minor argument with Dad out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty argument or tiff.

clue.text: Goes ahead and plays the star part

explanation.surface: An actor who gets in front and is cast as the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Moves into first place in a race, or is cast as the principal role in a play.

clue.text: The country's top people emerging from Heathrow?

explanation.surface: Aristocrats coming out of the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: people who have just touched down at London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Landowning upper class in rural Britain; also, whimsically, gentlefolk just arrived by plane.

clue.text: Drink from the basin

indicators.note: the drink is made from these letters, so the basin is rearranged to produce it

explanation.surface: Drinking something out of the washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is the anagram signal: the letters of THE BASIN are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: A green, aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood.

clue.text: Emile provides something fragrant

indicators.note: the name Emile supplies the raw letters, which are rearranged to give the fragrant thing

explanation.surface: A man named Emile brings along a pleasant scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant tree resin used in varnishes and incense.

clue.text: Anne's going out with North Polar explorer

indicators.note: the letters scatter as if leaving, so they are reordered

parts.note: the name with its S gives the letters to be rearranged
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Anne is off on a date with a man who explored the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' rearranges ANNES into NANSE, then N for North completes it. Fridtjof Nansen was a Norwegian Arctic explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian who led Arctic expeditions, notably crossing Greenland and drifting toward the Pole.

clue.text: Guns return, this animal may be hunted

indicators.note: the slang word for guns is turned back to front

parts.note: gats is slang for guns or pistols

explanation.surface: Shooters come back, because there is an animal to be hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, a traditional quarry of the hunt.

clue.text: The main picture

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea, so this is a painting of the ocean rather than the chief image

explanation.definitionFit: A painting or view of the ocean; 'the main' is literary for the open sea.

clue.text: One can't imagine being without them

definitions.text: One can't imagine being without them

parts.words: One can't imagine being without them
parts.note: sounds like something indispensable, but literally imagining is impossible without notions in the head

explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or notions, the raw material of imagination.

clue.text: Lilo is in decomposed state

indicators.note: broken down into parts, so the letters of Lilo is in are reassembled

explanation.surface: An airbed lies rotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decomposed' signals the anagram of LILO IS IN; a lilo is a British inflatable airbed. 'state' is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: They look and sound agreeable

indicators.note: the yes-votes are spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement, yeses

explanation.surface: People who look and sound pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: AYES (yes votes, from 'agreeable') said aloud gives the organs of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what do the looking.

clue.text: Travel overseas to get home

parts.note: not a journey back to one's house, but leaving one's country to find a new home abroad

explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's homeland permanently to settle in a foreign country.

clue.text: Unethical perfume brought back by pupil

indicators.note: the word for perfume is reversed, read from end to start

parts.note: an aroma is a scent or perfume
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A dodgy scent being returned by a schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns AROMA into AMORA, then L for pupil follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any moral sense, neither good nor bad by principle.

clue.text: Status symbols?

parts.note: usually luxury goods that show off wealth, here badges of rank or office worn on a uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Badges or emblems indicating rank, office or membership.

clue.text: A bad mark for the errant magistrates lacking rebuke

indicators.note: straying or wandering, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word for rebuke is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for to scold or rebuke them

explanation.surface: Magistrates who went astray, escaping a telling-off, get a black mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes RATES from MAGISTRATES leaving MAGIST, and 'errant' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of disgrace or shame attached to someone.

clue.text: Adjustment in damages

explanation.surface: Some correction in the amount of damages awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychologically, making up for a weakness; legally, money paid for loss or injury.

clue.text: Indicate a suitable victim

explanation.surface: Pointing out someone ripe for exploitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote or show something; also slang for an easy target of a con.

clue.text: Time to return to a region

indicators.note: the word for time is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It's time to go back to a certain district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses ERA to ARE, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A district, zone or tract of land.

clue.text: Knock back a portion of gin

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a part is a portion or share

explanation.surface: Downing a shot of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' (drink up, in the surface) reverses PART. 'gin' is not the spirit but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, as in a gin-trap.

clue.text: Sad pair evicted initially, having gone wrong here

definitions.text: Sad pair evicted initially, having gone wrong here

indicators.note: the letters of sad pair are scrambled as if things went awry
only the opening letter of evicted is used

explanation.surface: Adam and Eve, the unhappy couple thrown out of Eden after their sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone wrong' rearranges SAD PAIR to PARADIS, and 'initially' adds the E of 'evicted'. The whole clue describes the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden, the garden from which the first couple were expelled after the Fall.

clue.text: Carefully examines any seals broken

indicators.note: seals that are broken are disturbed, so the letters of any seals are reordered

explanation.surface: Inspecting documents for broken seals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals an anagram of ANY SEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Studies something in detail by breaking it into its parts.
